notes: Identity assessed directly: supplied canonical text is a full five-page primary Research Report, Running on Empty: Neural Signals for Self-Control Failure, Michael Inzlicht and Jennifer N. Gutsell, Psychological Science 18(11), 933–937, copyright 2007. Title, authors, year, journal, volume and pages agree with the reference. DOI is not printed in the supplied text and was not independently resolved. No PDF path supplied. The source describes a single unnumbered experiment, not a labeled Study 2. Page 935 (text page 3), Results—Behavioral Measures, reports one between-condition manipulation-check t test, not separate control-condition and suppression-condition tests. The assigned descriptions do not uniquely establish whether that common comparison or an unreported within-condition test is intended. No target was assigned from input order or numeric matching. Candidate common comparison: printed d = 1.10, t(31) = 3.05, prep = .97 (canonical parse uses 5 for the equals sign). prep is the printed replication-probability statistic, not an ordinary p value; no conversion performed. Candidate condition descriptives: suppression M = 5.03, SD = 1.69; control M = 3.11, SD = 1.89. Page 934, Subjects and Design, explicitly reports final suppression n = 15 and control n = 18, mutually exclusive randomly assigned groups; candidate common-comparison analytic N = 15 + 18 = 33 participants. Recruitment was 40; 7 excluded from all analyses for EEG artifacts (2), equipment malfunction (1), excessive incongruent Stroop error rates (3), or outlying EEG scores (1). Counts are candidates only because row-to-test correspondence remains unresolved; none are promoted to core values. Only original n, effect size and p fields assigned; other fields are placeholders.
